historical_record.description: The Mayor approved a schedule dedicating six new playgrounds of the 1947 recreation bond program, with the Joseph Lee recreation center, built as the Burnett Recreation Center, set for the evening of June 5.

Under the 1947 recreation bond program the Recreation Commission engaged William G. Merchant, architect, to design a field house at Burnett Playground, at the west end of the block of Oakdale, Mendell, Newcomb and Lane, on an estimated cost of $276,000.

The Recreation Commission awarded the contract to build the Burnett Recreation Center to Elvin C. Stendell for about $300,000, the lowest of four bids. At the same meeting it resolved that a future playground in the city bear the name of Joseph Lee, the Boston founder of the Playground Association of America.
The Recreation Commission named the Burnett project the Joseph Lee Recreation Center.
The Art Commission approved Dewey Crumpler's mural design for the gymnasium wall of the Joseph P. Lee recreation center.
